name: JTEKT India: Driving Precision, Powering India’s Mobility Future

market_expectation.valuation: P/E ratio ~18-20x on FY2025-26 EPS of Rs 2.84; trading at 9x historical growth rate. Valuation appears weak given near-term headwinds (margin compression, capacity ramp cycle).
market_expectation.growth_drivers: 11% revenue growth (FY25-26) outpaced market (9%); driven by Maruti Suzuki wins (e-Vitara, Victoris) and Brazil export startup. CVJ ramp underway (currently 27% utilized on Line 2, expected 90% when Maruti EV MPV launches Oct 26). Honda recovery expected post-new EV launch (Dec 26).
market_expectation.margin_outlook: EBITDA margins 7.6% (FY25-26) under near-term pressure from product mix (Honda -33% decline), US tariff hedges (recently reversed), and new-line ramp costs. Management expects recovery via export growth, capacity utilization, and tariff relief (US rate cut from 50% to 10%).

management_guidance.revenue: Incremental Rs 400-500 Cr expected FY26-27 from: (a) 10% market growth: Rs 400 Cr; (b) Export expansion (Brazil): Rs 75-100 Cr. Brazil ramp: 70k units FY26 → 100-150k units FY27 (potential Rs 50-60 Cr). Full CVJ capacity (2 lines) = Rs 250 Cr revenue at 90% utilization (triggered by Maruti EV MPV Oct 26).
management_guidance.capex: FY27: ~Rs 100 Cr incremental for Gujarat plant (total commitment Rs 250 Cr, already spent Rs 130 Cr). Capex declining vs FY25-26 (Rs 400+ Cr) as line-setup phase concludes; normal maintenance capex only going forward.
management_guidance.margin_recovery: Expects margin improvement via: (1) Export volume growth (Brazil, reduced US tariffs now 10% vs prior 50%); (2) Capacity utilization (new Maruti models fill existing lines); (3) Product mix normalization (Honda recovery post-EV launch Dec 26); (4) One-time cost headwinds (new-line testing, forex) expected to fade.

market_expectation_summary: JTEKT India is a niche, capital-intensive steering & CVJ (driveline) supplier to Maruti Suzuki (60% exposure), Toyota, and exports. Revenue grew 11% in FY25 to Rs 2,670 Cr; margins compressed to 7.6% EBITDA due to product mix headwinds (Honda -33%), US tariffs, and new-line ramp costs. Near-term catalysts: Maruti EV MPV launch (Oct 26) driving CVJ ramp to 90% utilization (Rs 250 Cr potential), Honda EV recovery (Dec 26), Brazil export ramp (70k→150k units), and US tariff relief now in effect. Management guides Rs 400-500 Cr incremental revenue and margin recovery as capacity fills. ROCE fell from 16% (FY24) to 10% (FY26) due to Rs 800 Cr capex over 3 years; recovery likely if revenue ramps and margins normalize.
guidance_history: FY2025-26 guidance (May 2026 call): (1) Revenue: Rs 2,600-2,700 Cr (delivered 2,670 Cr, up 11%); (2) EBITDA margin: 7.5-8.0% (delivered 7.6%, impacted by product mix and tariffs); (3) Export sales growth 20% (delivered, Rs 551 Cr → Rs 664 Cr). FY2026-27 outlook (management commentary, not formal guidance): Incremental Rs 400-500 Cr revenue, margin recovery via capacity utilization and tariff relief, Brazil export ramp to Rs 50-60 Cr. Capex to moderate to Rs 100-150 Cr (from Rs 400 Cr in FY26).
